chapter: Highlights, the reunion album and fellow musicians
title: Touring with the Ink Spots
summary: He took the Ink Spots on tour for $75 each before 'If I Didn't Care' was a hit.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Chicago. I went in with the Ink Spots for about 20 weeks tour. We played 20 weeks of nothing but theaters all over the country.

That's when the big record "If I Didn't Care" was out. Now, we had nothing but standing room only in all the theaters all during the tour. We was travelling by train. Anybody had, you know, could the Ink Spots in the sublet compartments, and we had Pullman cars for the rest of the band and everything. And then, we'd, the train, well, whatever time it was in, it would stop there and go back there and sleep there if we wanted to until the next day. We did tours, that was a beautiful tour. I can't forget that.

If you, this is something that you (inaudible). I was in Loew's State. I carried the Ink Spots in the Loew's State with me. Now, they was, their personal manager was the same as mine. And the come out with "If I Didn't Care".

Now, I'm in there. But, the number hadn't gotten prompted good. I goes in there and the manager asked me to take them in there on my act. So, I goes out (inaudible). I said sure. Now, all the money that I gave them. It was $75.00 apiece. They just wanted to get in there. Although the money not that big, it was pretty big during those days. Seventy-five dollars, you know?
So, they never got me when they got to be big. I mean, we just all got together and went on tours cause I gave them their first star bill.
"If I Didn't Care". In the next week or so, the biggest tune out.
